newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec's ex-Premier Robert Bourassa dies - report.
newsitem.headline: Quebec's ex-Premier Robert Bourassa dies - report.

text.p: Former Quebec Premier Robert Bourassa died early on Wednesday in a hospital in Montreal after a long battle with cancer, the French-language service of the Canadian Broadcasting Corp. reported.

Hospital officials did not immediately confirm Bourassa's death. The CBC said Bourassa, 63, died at 5:20 A.M. EDT (0920 GMT) at Notre-Dame Hospital. During his two terms as premier in the 1970s and 1980s, Bourassa was an ardent defender of Canadian unity and strove to keep Quebec in Canada.
The CBC said Bourassa was surrounded by friends and family, including his wife, Andree Simard, when he died.
Bourassa was admitted to the hospital in August, suffering from a relapse of skin cancer, which had spread to other parts of his body.

He resigned as premier in January 1994 because of his cancer. Bourassa's unexpected retirement may have helped clear the way for the separatist Parti Quebecois to win power in the provincial election later that year.
"If Quebec is still part of Canada today, it is because of Robert Bourassa," Claude Charon, a former Parti Quebecois cabinet minister told the CBC.
